raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview
Replaces the O(max_num_blocks) right-to-left scan in `SlidingWindowManager.find_longest_cache_hit` with a strided probe lattice, so low-hit-rate sliding-window requests skip uncached gaps. Also clamps the probe stride to 1 to avoid a non-terminating loop for `sliding_window=1` without EAGLE.

Fixes #62336. Related: #53276 — materially different, see Details.

## Claims
- 8192 -> 33 `get_cached_block` lookups for a 128K-token request with a 4K window and a cold cache (block_size=16); 4.49 ms -> 0.021 ms per call in the function-level harness (~200x).
- No regression for hit-heavy caches (256 -> 257 lookups; 0.23 ms -> 0.23 ms).
- Hit results are unchanged: exhaustive comparison with the previous implementation over 7,339,584 cases (all cached-block patterns up to 13 blocks, block sizes 1/2/4/8, windows 1-32, alignments 1-16, EAGLE on/off) plus 30,000 larger randomized cases (up to 4096 blocks) found 0 differences.
- Fixes a latent non-terminating loop for `sliding_window=1` without EAGLE.

## Validation
Environment: Python 3.12, torch 2.14.0+cu132, editable install with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty` (no compiled extensions needed for these CPU tests).

```bash
# New tests + full manager suite
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py -q
# 53 passed

# Related core suites
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_swa_inflight_window_free.py -q
# 240 passed, 1 failed on a transient Hugging Face download error;
# rerunning tests/v1/core/test_swa_inflight_window_free.py: 7 passed

# Connector path that reuses the same finder (lcm alignment, duck-typed pool)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_coordinator.py -q
# 38 passed

# Lint (ruff 0.14.0)
ruff check vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py
ruff format --check vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py
# All checks passed; 2 files already formatted
```

Function-level benchmark (`find_longest_cache_hit`, block_size=16, sliding_window=4096, 128K tokens, alignment=16, no EAGLE, lookups counted by wrapping `BlockPool.get_cached_block`):

| pattern | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| cold cache | 8192 lookups / 4.49 ms | 33 / 0.021 ms |
| 1% random cached | 8192 / 4.61 ms | 33 / 0.021 ms |
| tail hit / full cache | 256 / 0.23 ms | 257 / 0.23 ms |
| adversary (probes aligned with cached blocks) | 8192 / 4.63 ms | 128 / 0.11 ms |

No model evaluation is needed because the change does not affect output or accuracy. No end-to-end serving benchmark was run (the validation environment has no compiled vLLM extensions); reviewers may want a serving run before merge.

## Details

**Design.** A hit requires `stride = cdiv(sliding_window - 1, block_size) (+1 for EAGLE)` contiguous cached blocks. Probing every `stride`-th block from the right therefore cannot skip a candidate run, because any `stride` consecutive indices contain exactly one probe. Probe hits expand right (the next probe missed, so the run cannot extend past `i + stride - 1`) and verify only windows containing the probe. A miss at `idx` disqualifies every window ending in `(idx, edge]`, so the search resumes at the next aligned edge below `idx - 1`. Alignment retries use `alignment_tokens // gcd(alignment_tokens, block_size)`.

**Why this is not a duplicate of #53276.** #53276 (open since 2026-08-21, no human review activity) adds a left-boundary lookahead only for the current-block miss case and otherwise still advances one block at a time; alignment retries stay per-block, the prefix fallback still comes from the full scan, and it adds no tests. This PR replaces the loop, is proven not to skip candidates, handles the alignment-period and right-expansion cases, and ships an equivalence test plus a zero-stride regression test. See the linked issue for the full comparison.

**Root cause of the zero-stride fix.** `_contiguous_blocks_for_hit` returns `cdiv(sliding_window - 1, block_size) == 0` for a one-token window when EAGLE is disabled. The new probe loop uses that value as its step, so `i -= stride` would not advance. Clamping to 1 reproduces the previous scan's behavior: a single cached block can still be reused, and a cold cache terminates with an empty hit. `_contiguous_blocks_for_hit` itself is unchanged because it is also used by `reachable_block_mask`, whose semantics depend on the raw value.

**Tradeoffs / limitations.**
- Worst case remains O(max_num_blocks), e.g. when cached blocks are arranged on the probe lattice; measured 128 lookups vs 8192 today.
- One dict of at most `stride` entries is allocated on a hit.
- Hit-heavy paths are unchanged within one lookup.
- Validation is unit/function-level, not end-to-end serving.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.
- [x] **Design Fit:** The change is local to `SlidingWindowManager`, reuses the existing `_contiguous_blocks_for_hit` definition, and adds no dependencies.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Randomized equivalence test, zero-stride regression test, full manager suite, and related core suites pass; benchmark and reproduction are provided above. CI runs this as a CPU test.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass; no unrelated formatting changes.

@@ -630,6 +630,133 @@ def run_one_case(block_is_cached, expect_length):
     )
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("drop_eagle_block", [False, True])
+def test_sliding_window_cache_hit_matches_brute_force(drop_eagle_block):
+    """The strided probe search must find the same window as a full scan."""
+    block_size = 2
+    sliding_window = 8
+    sliding_window_spec = SlidingWindowSpec(
+        block_size=block_size,
+        num_kv_heads=1,
+        head_size=1,
+        dtype=torch.float32,
+        sliding_window=sliding_window,
+    )
+    # Twice the block size, so the search has to retry with an alignment step.
+    alignment_tokens = 2 * block_size
+    block_pool = BlockPool(
+        num_gpu_blocks=200, enable_caching=True, hash_block_size=block_size
+    )
+    manager = get_sliding_window_manager(sliding_window_spec, block_pool)
+    need = SlidingWindowManager._contiguous_blocks_for_hit(
+        sliding_window, block_size, drop_eagle_block
+    )
+    # A hit may only end on a block aligned with `alignment_tokens`.
+    align_shift = 0 if drop_eagle_block else 1
+
+    def is_aligned(edge: int) -> bool:
+        return ((edge + align_shift) * block_size) % alignment_tokens == 0
+
+    def find_longest(block_is_cached):
+        block_hash_list = [
+            BlockHash(str(i).encode()) for i in range(len(block_is_cached))
+        ]
+        block_pool.cached_block_hash_to_block._cache.clear()
+        for i, block_hash in enumerate(block_hash_list):
+            if block_is_cached[i]:
+                block_pool.cached_block_hash_to_block.insert(
+                    make_block_hash_with_group_id(block_hash, 0),
+                    block_pool.blocks[i + 10],
+                )
+        computed_blocks, hit_length = manager.find_longest_cache_hit(
+            block_hashes=block_hash_list,
+            max_length=len(block_hash_list) * block_size,
+            kv_cache_group_ids=[0],
+            block_pool=block_pool,
+            kv_cache_spec=sliding_window_spec,
+            drop_eagle_block=drop_eagle_block,
+            alignment_tokens=alignment_tokens,
+        )
+        return computed_blocks[0], hit_length
+
+    rng = random.Random(0)
+    for _ in range(200):
+        num_blocks = rng.randint(0, 24)
+        cache_prob = rng.choice([0.2, 0.5, 0.8, 1.0])
+        block_is_cached = [rng.random() < cache_prob for _ in range(num_blocks)]
+        computed_blocks, hit_length = find_longest(block_is_cached)
+
+        assert hit_length == len(computed_blocks) * block_size
+        assert hit_length % alignment_tokens == 0
+        # Reused blocks are cached; skipped blocks stay null.
+        assert all(
+            block == block_pool.null_block or block_is_cached[block.block_id - 10]
+            for block in computed_blocks
+        )
+
+        # Brute force: the rightmost aligned run of `need` cached blocks.
+        best_edge = next(
+            (
+                edge
+                for edge in range(num_blocks - 1, need - 2, -1)
+                if is_aligned(edge) and all(block_is_cached[edge - need + 1 : edge + 1])
+            ),
+            None,
+        )
+        if best_edge is None:
+            # No run is long enough: the hit is a (aligned) cached prefix.
+            assert computed_blocks == [
+                block for block in computed_blocks if block != block_pool.null_block
+            ]
+            continue
+        # EAGLE drops the last matched block, so the hit ends one block early.
+        assert len(computed_blocks) == best_edge + align_shift
+        last = min(best_edge + 1, len(computed_blocks))
+        for i in range(best_edge - need + 1, last):
+            assert computed_blocks[i].block_id == i + 10
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("cached_block", [None, 4])
+def test_sliding_window_single_token_window(cached_block):
+    """A one-token window needs no contiguous blocks; the probe loop must
+    terminate and reuse a single cached block."""
+    block_size = 2
+    num_blocks = 8
+    sliding_window_spec = SlidingWindowSpec(
+        block_size=block_size,
+        num_kv_heads=1,
+        head_size=1,
+        dtype=torch.float32,
+        sliding_window=1,
+    )
+    block_pool = BlockPool(
+        num_gpu_blocks=100, enable_caching=True, hash_block_size=block_size
+    )
+    manager = get_sliding_window_manager(sliding_window_spec, block_pool)
+    block_hashes = [BlockHash(str(i).encode()) for i in range(num_blocks)]
+    if cached_block is not None:
+        block_pool.cached_block_hash_to_block.insert(
+            make_block_hash_with_group_id(block_hashes[cached_block], 0),
+            block_pool.blocks[10],
+        )
+
+    computed_blocks, hit_length = manager.find_longest_cache_hit(
+        block_hashes=block_hashes,
+        max_length=num_blocks * block_size,
+        kv_cache_group_ids=[0],
+        block_pool=block_pool,
+        kv_cache_spec=sliding_window_spec,
+        drop_eagle_block=False,
+        alignment_tokens=block_size,
+    )
+
+    expected_blocks = 0 if cached_block is None else cached_block + 1
+    assert hit_length == expected_blocks * block_size
+    assert len(computed_blocks[0]) == expected_blocks
+    if cached_block is not None:
+        assert computed_blocks[0][cached_block] is block_pool.blocks[10]
+

+        computed_blocks: tuple[list[KVCacheBlock], ...] = tuple(
+            [block_pool.null_block] * min(hits, default=0)

-            for computed in computed_blocks:
